name: The Godhead (LDS)
dom: supreme divinity; tritheistic unity of purpose
note: Canonical (Articles of Faith 1; D&C 130:22): three distinct personages — Father, Son, Holy Ghost — one in purpose, not one substance. Cohort hub.

name: Heavenly Father (Elohim)
dom: exalted embodied Father of spirits; supreme God
note: Attested in LDS scripture and temple usage; an exalted, embodied, anthropomorphic God who was once a man (Givens, Wrestling the Angel). Distinct LDS conception, not the classical Trinity's Father.

name: Heavenly Mother
dom: divine feminine; mother of spirits; consort of Heavenly Father
note: Officially affirmed (Gospel Topics essay 'Mother in Heaven'; Eliza R. Snow hymn 'O My Father'); divine consort and co-parent of premortal spirits (Givens, Wrestling the Angel).

name: Jehovah / Jesus Christ (LDS)
dom: premortal Jehovah, creator under the Father, incarnate Redeemer
note: LDS framing identifies the premortal Jehovah of the Old Testament with Jesus Christ, the Firstborn spirit and Son who created the worlds under the Father (Givens; Bible Dictionary, 'Jehovah'). Cross-links to existing ENT_JESUS_CHRIST as the LDS reception.

name: Holy Ghost (LDS)
dom: third member of the Godhead; personage of spirit; witness/revelator
note: Canonical (D&C 130:22): a personage of spirit without a body of flesh, distinct from the Father and Son. LDS reception of the Christian Holy Spirit.

name: Premortal Spirit Existence (Pre-existence)
dom: premortal life of spirits as God's children before birth
note: Doctrine of premortal existence: all humans lived as spirit children of Heavenly Parents before mortal birth (Givens; Book of Abraham 3; D&C 93:29).

name: Council in Heaven
dom: premortal divine council on the plan of salvation
note: Premortal council where the Father presented the plan of salvation; Jesus and Lucifer offered competing roles, leading to the War in Heaven (Book of Abraham 3; Book of Moses 4; Givens).

name: Michael / Adam (LDS)
dom: archangel Michael who became Adam, the first man and Ancient of Days
note: Canonical identification (D&C 27:11; 107:54; 116): the archangel Michael is Adam, the first man, the 'Ancient of Days' who presides over his posterity. Cross-links to existing Adam and Michael anchors as LDS reception.

name: Moroni (Angel)
dom: resurrected Nephite prophet; angelic revealer of the golden plates
note: Joseph Smith—History (Pearl of Great Price): last Nephite prophet-historian, resurrected as the angel who revealed and delivered the golden plates from which the Book of Mormon was translated.

name: Lucifer / Perdition (LDS)
dom: premortal Son of the Morning who rebelled and became Satan
note: Book of Moses 4 and D&C 76:25–27: a spirit son of God in the premortal council who sought to supplant the plan and was cast out, becoming the devil and the sons of perdition.

name: Kolob
dom: the star/realm nearest to the throne of God
note: Book of Abraham 3 and Facsimile 2: the great star/governing body nearest to where God resides, governing in time and order; a realm in LDS cosmology.

name: Three Degrees of Glory
dom: the tripartite kingdoms of eternal reward
note: D&C 76: the three postmortal kingdoms (Celestial, Terrestrial, Telestial) into which resurrected souls are assigned by glory; parent category of the three kingdoms.

name: Celestial Kingdom
dom: highest degree of glory; dwelling of God and the exalted
note: D&C 76:50–70, 131: the highest kingdom, where God and Christ dwell and where the exalted may attain godhood; likened to the glory of the sun.

name: Terrestrial Kingdom
note: D&C 76:71–80: the middle kingdom for honorable people who did not receive the fulness of the gospel; likened to the glory of the moon.

name: Telestial Kingdom
note: D&C 76:81–90: the lowest of the three kingdoms of glory; likened to the glory of the stars.

name: Exaltation (Theosis)
dom: becoming gods; eternal increase in the Celestial Kingdom
note: Doctrine of exaltation/divinization: faithful Saints may attain godhood and eternal family increase (Lorenzo Snow couplet; D&C 132; Givens, Wrestling the Angel). LDS form of theosis.

name: Plan of Salvation
dom: the divine plan of premortal, mortal, and postmortal progression
note: The overarching LDS doctrinal framework presented at the Council in Heaven, encompassing premortal life, mortality, and the degrees of glory (Givens; Book of Abraham 3).
